analysis:
This PR changes only the CI threat-review tooling under .github/scripts/threat_review. It does not touch provider, coordinator, attestation, encryption or cache code, so no provider threat (TB-002/003/007/009/011, T-041, T-053) is directly affected. The tooling is the process that gates review of those threats, so I examined it for weakened review or clearance.

bedrock.py:46-84 adds a 'workload' call policy. It plans calls per stage, allows one shared repair slot, and has an emergency ceiling of 500 (cap 500). When the plan exceeds the ceiling, it raises BudgetStopped. In workload mode the default output tokens rise to 16384. These are cost and availability changes. Accounting stops on missing usage (lines 204-208) and fallback (lines 98-110) are unchanged.

budget_runner.py:
- Lines 38-48 add a human-review banner for incomplete or failed runs and a 'Scan completed.' line. The clearance predicate 'complete' (lines 26-29) is unchanged.
- Lines 175-177 make run attempts other than 1 fail closed.
- Line 225 marks the run as finished on exceptions.
The new banners do not loosen clearance.

budget_scan.py:
- The path-regex RISK/CRITICAL escalation is replaced by depth_policy.source_depth. That module is not supplied, so I cannot verify that critical paths (provider crypto, attestation, KVCacheSSD) still escalate.
- When integration returns findings or high-severity findings, depth review no longer covers all source batches. It now covers only batches cited by self.findings via finding_batches (lines 330-338, 350-353).
- Outside force_deep mode, critical batches no longer also get an Opus pass (lines 371-375).
- If integration findings that cite lines outside retained source findings never enter self.findings, those cross-file issues get no depth pass. Integration's needs_deeper_review still adds a manual-review reason, which preserves human gating.

These changes reduce review depth but are not a demonstrated security regression of the in-scope assets.

Open questions for integration:
- Does source_depth retain critical-path escalation?
- Does self.findings include integration-stage findings?
- Can finding_batches raise KeyError on an unexpected side or file? That would be fail-closed via the error path.
